payload.definition: Jokes that reference obsolete technology, defunct platforms, expired cultural moments, or outdated social norms that mark when the joke was created or will become unfamiliar to new audiences.
payload.inclusion_criteria: Explicit mention of technology no longer in widespread use (fax, dial-up, flip phones, CDs, early internet platforms), defunct companies or services, specific celebrities or cultural moments tied to a particular era, or social practices that have shifted.
payload.exclusion_criteria: General references that remain current (computers, social media as ongoing category, universal human experiences). Technology mentioned as still-functional or timeless.
examples: Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs. (If 'bugs' referenced specific outdated bug types or extinct software)
A man tells his doctor, 'Help me. I'm addicted to Twitter!' (Twitter's cultural dominance is now contested; may age)
References to fax machines, AOL, Myspace, flip phones, dial-up internet
counter_examples: Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field. (Timeless, no reference frame)
What do you call a fish wearing a bowtie? Sofishticated. (Wordplay, no temporal marker)
